the ORISCAVA-LUX2 study sample was not fully representative of the Luxembourgish national population, and the sample was not fully comparable to baseline sample in terms of socio-demographic characteristics, health status and risk profile.

the ORISCAVA-LUX sample is representative of the national population in terms of geographical district, but it is not in terms of sex and age; and that it includes participants with better health perception, lower prevalence of obesity and related biomarkers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sampling strategy that is flexible enough to accommodate changes during the course of the project and that can be adapted to the specific needs of the project.
the challenges and benefits of integrating different sampling strategies in the ORISCAVA-LUX 2 study.
the integration of different sampling strategies in a single epidemiological survey.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ORISCA-LUX2 sample is representative of the Luxembourgish population for geographical district and sex, but not for age.
the ORISCAVLUX2 sample is a representative sample of the Luxembourg population, with some underrepresentation of the younger and older population.
the sample is representative in terms of age and sex for geographical district and representative of national population in terms of education, health status and cardiometabolic risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ORISCA-V-LUX 2 sample is not a simple replication of the baseline sample, but a new sample with a different composition and health status.

the ORISCA-VLUX2 sample was a representative sample of the population of Luxembourg, with a good coverage of the target population, and that the sample was representative of the general population in terms of age, sex, geographical district, and socioeconomic status.
the ORISCA-LUX2 dataset is a valuable resource for epidemiological research, health monitoring and prevention in Luxembourg.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a careful and thoughtful design of sampling strategy and data collection plan, as well as a clear and transparent description of the sample characteristics, are crucial in order to avoid misinterpretation of the results.
it is possible to create a complementary sample to a baseline population-based study, by combining different sampling strategies.
the integration of diverse sampling strategies can be a solution to increase the representativeness of the sample.
